messages:
lee (Sales): FYI procurement at MedAxis returned our OF with two hard asks: DocuSign ID Check mandatory for all signers, and a 99.9% uptime SLA with slide-scale credits up to 15% monthly. This is a 3-month dedicated POC (~$52k). Thoughts on leaning in vs pushback?

anita (Legal): Paste their exact redlines if you have them. Quick take: notarization and high credit caps are non-starters for short POCs. We usually offer a POC-specific SLA and limit credits to POC fees.

lee (Sales): Verbatim: "Provider must require e-sign identity verification (DocuSign ID Check) for each signer. Provider warrants 99.9% service availability; for each 0.1% below, Customer may claim service credits up to 15% of monthly fees."

omar (Solutions): We can enable the DocuSign ID Check in the envelope. Dedicated mini-pool can be created in ~5 business days. However small pools have higher variance; committing 99.9% is risky for short windows.

paul (Engineering): Agreed. Our Dedicated standard contract for committed capacity is 99.5% with graduated credits. For POCs we prefer 99.5% and a cap equal to the POC fee. Also need to define what counts as downtime (inference server vs control plane/API).

anita (Legal): Proposed counter language for the OF: "For Proof-of-Concepts, Provider offers a 99.5% uptime SLA. Service credits for POCs are limited to the aggregate fees paid for the POC term. Provider accepts electronic signatures via DocuSign; DocuSign ID Check satisfies Provider's signer authentication requirements. Provider is not liable for third-party ID verification failures." Any objections?

rachel (Finance): Fine with capping credits to POC fees. If Sales wants concessions, Finance can authorize a one-time conversion credit equal to 7.5% of POC fees (paid as credit against future committed spend) if Customer signs an annual Dedicated commitment within 45 days of POC end. Need exact fee to compute dollar cap.

lee (Sales): Procurement will insist on dollar amounts. I'll confirm the $52k and see if notarization is demanded beyond DocuSign. If they insist on notarization for >$250k we can require a paper path, but this POC is below that threshold.

docusign-bot: Template created: "Redwood POC OF" (tpl-9001). Recommend Auth: ID Check when enabled.

paul (Engineering): I'll draft a short SLA carveout to attach: scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice, customer-caused outages, and force majeure excluded. Also clarify measurement method (rolling 30-day window vs monthly).

anita (Legal): Good. I'll prepare a redline with the 99.5% POC SLA, credit cap, DocuSign clause, and the conversion credit language. Uploading to the ticket by COB.

lee (Sales): Thanks. Routing plan: DocuSign envelope to include procurement approver + legal on customer side, our AE, and Anita as countersigner. Rachel, please calculate the dollar cap once I confirm final fee. If procurement presses notarization again I'll escalate to legal. :thumbsup:

rachel (Finance): Will compute caps after final fee confirmed. Prefer absolute dollar caps in OF for clarity.

lee (Sales): Closing loop: push redline, provision template with ID Check off by default and enable on acceptance, and hold spin-up until OF countersigned. Thanks team.
